private_lines.Marcus: You raked the sodden leaves off the lawn once the rain eased, then drove to the garden centre on Roundhay Road for a bag of tulip bulbs and a new pair of secateurs. Your wife made you stay for lunch in the conservatory, and you spent the afternoon planting the bulbs along the back border while the light lasted.

private_lines.Dev: The match finished 3–1 to your side, and your youngest scored the second goal off a scramble before spending the drive home explaining the tactics to anyone within earshot. This afternoon you took the children swimming at the baths on Otley Road while your partner stayed home to wrap presents, and by teatime you had put the Christmas lights up along the front of the house. Tonight it's fish and chips and a film the children chose, which you are not allowed to change.

private_lines.Hannah: You were out on the longer loop past the locks before eight, with the towpath still cold and damp, and the miles felt easier than they have in weeks. Back home you showered, had a late breakfast, and spent the afternoon tidying the flat before your sister's visit: hoovering, changing the bedding, clearing out the spare room. By evening you'd finished, eaten a bowl of pasta, and settled in on the sofa with the telly on.

private_lines.Sophie: You made porridge with Priya once she woke, then took the bus to the leisure centre and got a full thirty minutes on the bike, the first time in three weeks. Back home you did a load of washing, read a chapter in the front room, and ordered a Chinese takeaway for the evening.

private_lines.Marcus: You finished planting the last of the tulip bulbs by torchlight, then scrubbed the mud off your hands before the kitchen got busy. Dinner was the chicken and leek pie your wife had been planning all week, eaten with the radio on while the rain started again against the conservatory glass. By half nine you were on the sofa with a mug of tea, half-watching the football highlights and not caring who won.
